contradiction_resolution: There are no registered claim-level contradictions and FND-0128 is absent from the packet's corroborated findings because pending candidates are quarantined. Primary sources nevertheless contradict two clauses of its literal formulation: unramified does not by itself imply etale without flatness, and connected reduced does not make a nonempty open schematically dense. After replacing those clauses by unramified and integral-or-schematically-dense respectively, the sections proof is valid and establishes the campaign's smooth connected-curve application.

corrected_mathematical_scope.campaign_application: For the campaign's smooth connected geometric genus-six curve, C is integral, so the corrected argument proves the required stabilizer rigidity.
corrected_mathematical_scope.counterexample_to_original_generality: Take two copies C1 and C2 of P^1 glued at infinity. Let gamma restrict to the identity on C1 and to z|->z^2 on C2, and let sigma be the identity on C1 and z|->-z on C2. Then C is connected and reduced, sigma is a nonidentity automorphism over P^1, and every finite point x of C1 is fixed with gamma unramified at x. Thus local equality does not propagate across arbitrary connected reduced C.
corrected_mathematical_scope.cross_checked_claims: No contradiction with CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. The finding is complementary to the packet's stabilizer and stack-scope findings FND-0060, FND-0075, FND-0086, and FND-0127.
corrected_mathematical_scope.degree_scope: The rigidity lemma is independent of the degree of gamma; degree four is only the campaign application.

local_argument: The first projection C x_{P^1} C -> C is the base change of gamma, so it is unramified at (x,x).
The identity and sigma graphs are sections meeting at (x,x). The open-diagonal property of an unramified morphism makes their equalizer an open neighborhood of x.
Finiteness supplies separatedness. Equality on that neighborhood extends globally when it is schematically dense.
required_corrections: Replace connected reduced by integral, reduced irreducible, or an explicit schematic-density hypothesis. A nonempty open subset of a connected reduced reducible curve need not be dense in every component.

Replace 'pr_1 is etale because gamma is unramified at x' by 'pr_1 is unramified at (x,x)'. Etaleness additionally requires flatness. In the actual smooth-curve finite-cover setting flatness is available, but it is unnecessary for the section argument.
Interpret sigma(x)=x as equality at the relevant geometric point, ensuring the two sections meet as points of the fiber product.
corrected_mathematical_scope.statement: Let gamma:C->P^1 be finite, let sigma be a P^1-automorphism of C, and let x be a geometric point such that sigma fixes x and gamma is unramified at x. If C is integral, or more generally the neighborhood on which sigma equals the identity is schematically dense in C, then sigma is the identity.
